title_en: Liu Yongmin and Liu Yongyou v. Beipiao Mining Bureau and Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory — dispute over patent application rights
keywords_en: civil; dispute over patent application rights; first instance; intermediate people's court; Liaoning Province; natural person; legal person; patent law; determination of service invention and non-service invention; determination of inventor qualification; partial support; fan modification; service invention; patent application right; dispute over patent application right of mining machinery factory
full_text_en:
Liu Yongmin and Liu Yongyou v. Beipiao Mining Bureau and
Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory — Dispute over Patent Application Right

Plaintiff: Liu Yongmin, male, 62 years old, former Chief Engineer of the Collective Enterprise General Company of Beipiao Mining Bureau, Liaoning Province (now retired).
Agent ad litem: Chen Yubin, lawyer of the Second Law Firm of Shenyang City, Liaoning Province.

Plaintiff: Liu Yongyou, male, 52 years old, Head of the Power Section of Jinzhou Food Factory, Liaoning Province.
Agent ad litem: Li Zongjin, engineer of Liaoning Provincial Foreign Science and Technology Exchange Company.

Defendant: Beipiao Mining Bureau, Liaoning Province.
Legal representative: Yu Binnian, Director.
Agent ad litem: Dong Xin, Director of the Legal Advisory Office of Beipiao Mining Bureau.

Defendant: Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory, Liaoning Province.
Legal representative: Feng Zhenfu, Factory Manager.
Agent ad litem: Lang Jichang, Deputy Factory Manager of Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory, Liaoning Province.

Plaintiffs Liu Yongmin and Liu Yongyou filed a lawsuit with the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province regarding a dispute over patent application right with Beipiao Mining Bureau and Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory.

The plaintiffs Liu Yongmin and Liu Yongyou alleged: "Mine Axial Flow Fan" was a scientific research achievement persistently conducted by the plaintiffs in their spare time. This invention was a non-service invention. They requested the court to confirm that the patent application right for this invention belonged to the plaintiffs.

The defendants Beipiao Mining Bureau and Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory argued: According to Article 6 and Article 8 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 10 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, this invention should be a service invention, and the patent application right should belong to the defendants. Liu Yongmin was one of the inventors of this invention, while Liu Yongyou was not an employee of the defendant units and did not participate in the inventive work. Therefore, he was not eligible to be an inventor or an applicant.

After public trial, the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court found the following facts:

From September 1978 to February 1980, the plaintiff Liu Yongmin served as an engineer in the Mechanical and Electrical Department of Beipiao Mining Bureau. During this period, Liu Yongmin participated in fan transformation and was responsible for technical work, successively developing "Beipiao Type 1, 2, 3, and 4 Blades." Among them, the Type 4 twisted blade reached the domestic advanced level. In 1979, the Liaoning Provincial Coal Administration arranged for Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory to trial-produce the Type 4 twisted blade, and Liu Yongmin was dispatched by the unit to be responsible for the technical work of the trial production. Liu Yongmin, using both working and spare time, participated together with Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory in the trial production of blades and the transformation of fans. In March 1980, after Liu Yongmin was transferred to Sanbao Mine as Deputy Chief Mechanical and Electrical Engineer, he still frequently went to the factory to participate in resolving related technical issues of the trial production. In July 1980, the Ministry of Coal Industry allocated RMB 150,000 to establish a fan test station at Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory. In June of the same year, Shenyang Blower Factory developed the 2K60 mine axial flow fan. The Liaoning Provincial Coal Administration decided to test this fan at Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory and appointed Liu Yongmin as the head of the test team. Based on years of experience in fan transformation and drawing on advanced foreign technology, Liu Yongmin promptly conceived a transformed fan and carried out preliminary design. At the beginning of January 1982, the technical scheme for the design principles and main parameter selection of the 2KDB-55-1 mine axial flow ventilator (mainly focusing on transforming the impeller) was determined. On March 12 of the same year, the Production Department of the Ministry of Coal Industry decided that the Ministry of Coal Industry would provide funding, Liu Yongmin would be responsible for the technology, and Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory would be responsible for trial-producing the transformed 2KDB-55-1 mine axial flow fan. In October of the same year, the prototype trial production was completed and tested at the fan test station of Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory. On November 2 of the same year, the Ministry of Coal Industry commissioned the Liaoning Provincial Coal Administration to hold an evaluation meeting at Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory, which considered that the fan could be finalized for industrial testing and technical appraisal when conditions permitted.

In June 1983, the Ministry of Coal Industry allocated RMB 70,000 as test funds. In May 1985, at a technical appraisal meeting for the transformed 2KDB-55-1 mine axial flow ventilator commissioned by the Ministry of Coal Industry and organized by the Northeast Coal Corporation, it was determined that the developing units of the fan were Beipiao Mining Bureau and Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory. On May 12, 1987, Liu Yongmin and his younger brother Liu Yongyou jointly filed a utility model patent application for a non-service invention entitled "Mine Axial Flow Fan" with the Chinese Patent Office (Application No. 87023256). On November 4, 1988, the defendants Beipiao Mining Bureau and Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory submitted a request to the Liaoning Provincial Patent Administration for mediation of the dispute over patent application right on the ground that "Mine Axial Flow Fan" was a service invention. On June 4, 1990, the Liaoning Provincial Patent Administration issued a decision that the applicant Liu Yongmin's invention was a non-service invention and that Liu Yongyou was not qualified as a patent applicant. Liu Yongmin and Liu Yongyou, dissatisfied with this decision, filed a lawsuit with the court on the ground that their patent was a non-service invention.

The Shenyang Intermediate People's Court held: Since 1987, the plaintiff Liu Yongmin had successively served as Mechanical and Electrical Engineer of Beipiao Mining Bureau, Deputy Chief Mechanical and Electrical Engineer of Sanbao Mine, and Chief Engineer of the General Mechanical and Electrical Factory of Beipiao Mining Bureau. He was responsible for the management, maintenance, and transformation of ventilators, which are large-scale general mechanical and electrical equipment in coal mines. During the process of ventilator transformation, Liu Yongmin, based on his practical experience and combined with advanced foreign technology, creatively carried out fan transformation. Together with the trial production of the 2KDB-55-1 fan, he proposed the technical scheme for "Mine Axial Flow Fan" and made outstanding contributions to the trial production and transformation of the fan. During the trial production and transformation process, the Ministry of Coal Industry and the Liaoning Provincial Coal Administration allocated trial production funds, and the defendants Beipiao Mining Bureau and Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory invested human and material resources. In accordance with Article 6, paragraph 1 of the Patent Law: "For a service invention-creation made by an employee in the execution of the tasks of the employee's own unit or made mainly by using the material conditions of the unit, the right to apply for a patent belongs to the unit." The creation of "Mine Axial Flow Fan" by Liu Yongmin was a service invention-creation. The right to apply for a patent for this technology should belong to Beipiao Mining Bureau and Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory. In accordance with Article 11 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law, Liu Yongmin made creative contributions to the substantive features of the creation of "Mine Axial Flow Fan" and was an inventor of this fan technology. In accordance with Article 16 of the Patent Law, the unit that made a service invention-creation shall reward the inventor. In the process of creating "Mine Axial Flow Fan," the plaintiff Liu Yongyou provided technical materials to the inventor Liu Yongmin and participated in some discussions, but he did not make creative contributions to the invention-creation of this technology. In accordance with Article 11 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law, persons who provided convenience for the use of material conditions or engaged in other auxiliary work during the completion of the invention-creation shall not be considered inventors.

After clarifying the facts and distinguishing right from wrong, the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court conducted mediation, and on January 24, 1992, both parties voluntarily reached the following agreement:

1. The plaintiff Liu Yongmin agrees that "Mine Axial Flow Fan" is a service invention-creation, and the patent application right is jointly owned by the defendants Beipiao Mining Bureau and Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory.

2. The plaintiff Liu Yongmin is the inventor of the invention-creation "Mine Axial Flow Fan"; the plaintiff Liu Yongyou cannot be considered an inventor or a patent applicant for this invention-creation.

3. After the mediation agreement takes effect, Beipiao Mining Machinery Factory agrees to pay the plaintiffs Liu Yongmin and Liu Yongyou a one-time bonus and labor remuneration of RMB 20,000.

4. After the mediation agreement takes effect, the plaintiffs and defendants shall not pursue any liability against each other regarding any patent transfer or implementation conducted before the agreement takes effect. After the agreement takes effect, the patent applicant's production or transfer of this product shall no longer require economic compensation to the plaintiff Liu Yongmin.
